🎓 Built with Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham — Live-in-Labs®
GeoRoots turns informal field knowledge into a structured, exportable civic dataset — crowd-sourced, geotagged points covering infrastructure, utilities, resources, and hazards, synced in real time so any team member, local authority, or researcher can read from and build on the same map.
🏔️ Hill Station & Disaster Ops
Live operating snapshot computed from community-logged points within 15km of the current view / GNSS position. Designed for landslide-prone terrain such as the Nilgiris, Kolli Hills, Kodaikanal, Yercaud — and generalizes to any hill terrain (e.g. Uttarkashi) once local field teams start logging points there.

About Amrita
Amrita Live-in-Labs® — community event, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham is a multi-campus private university headquartered in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, and deemed a university under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. Founded under the guidance of Sri Mata Amritanandamayi Devi (Amma), it runs campuses across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh, with schools spanning engineering, medicine, business, and the humanities, alongside an active research and sustainable-development agenda recognised internationally, including a UNESCO Chair for Experiential Learning.
Where This Idea Came From
GeoRoots grew out of Amrita Live-in-Labs® — Amrita's flagship experiential-learning program that sends students to live directly in rural communities across India. Living alongside a community surfaced a persistent problem: no one had a reliable, shared record of where water points, road damage, drainage, and hazards actually were on the ground.

GeoRoots was built to close that gap — a way for any field team to log real infrastructure with GNSS accuracy and get it into a shared map the moment it's captured. The app grew from field experience, not a classroom, and that's what it's built for.
